title: What Wadsworth schools’ proposed 1% earned income tax would cover
dek: The November 3 vote concerns a five-year tax on district residents’ earned income.
body:
Wadsworth City School District voters face a proposed 1% earned income tax for five years on November 3, 2026. For households weighing the cost, the district’s tax explanation includes wages, salaries, tips and self-employment income from sole proprietorships and partnerships, to the extent included in modified adjusted gross income.

The district says retirement income, interest, dividends, capital gains and unemployment benefits are excluded. The tax would be paid by district residents if approved.

The financial context predates this election: the district’s August forecast projected that cash reserves would run out in fiscal year 2029 without changes. The district says it is reviewing staffing and service reductions alongside the tax proposal. That forecast is a projection, not an existing cash shortfall.

editorial.residentValue: Helps voters understand the proposed tax’s duration, covered income and financial context before deciding.
editorial.change: An upcoming vote on a five-year, 1% earned income tax provides a timely reason to explain existing financial background.
editorial.whyNow: The November 3, 2026 election is 29 days after the edition cutoff.

evidenceRefs.assertion: The district proposes a 1% earned income tax for five years at the November 3, 2026 election; the proposal awaits voters.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Request: 1.0% Earned Income Tax
                              Duration: A Period of Five (5) Years
                                 Election: November 3, 2026

evidenceRefs.assertion: Covered earned income includes wages, salaries, tips and self-employment income from sole proprietorships and partnerships to the extent included in modified adjusted gross income; the listed retirement and investment income and unemployment benefits are excluded.
evidenceRefs.quote:
“Earned income includes only the following items to the extent that they are included in your
modified adjusted gross income (MAGI):
   - Employee compensation, such as wages, salaries, and tips; and
   - Self-employment income from sole proprietorships and partnerships.

Earned income does not include items such as retirement income, interest, dividends and
capital gains, and unemployment benefits.”

evidenceRefs.assertion: District residents would pay the earned income tax if voters approve it.
evidenceRefs.quote:
If approved, the earned income tax is paid by residents of the Wadsworth City School District,
as outlined in the question above.

evidenceRefs.assertion: The financial projection dates to August 2026.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Fiscal Year 2027 – Four-Year Projection
                                 August 2026

evidenceRefs.assertion: The district projected depletion of cash reserves in fiscal year 2029 without changes and said it was reviewing staffing and service reductions alongside the proposed tax.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Without change,
we anticipate that our cash reserves will be depleted in FY 2029. For that reason, the Board of
Education continues to review reductions in staffing and services to reduce expenditures, and has
placed a 1% earned income tax for a period of five years on the November 3, 2026, ballot.

title: Chick-fil-A project behind Sheetz received access-road approval in August
dek: Wadsworth City Council adopted the access-road and utility-easement ordinance tied to the proposed Chick-fil-A on August 3, 2026. The site is directly west of Sheetz, where the Legacy Inn had been located.
body:
Wadsworth City Council adopted the access-road and utility-easement ordinance tied to the proposed Chick-fil-A on August 3, 2026. The site is directly west of Sheetz, where the Legacy Inn had been located.

Ordinance 26-082 accepted public right of way for Access Road One and utility easements on the subdivision plat for city lot 10300. The Planning Commission approved that plat June 8. Council adopted the ordinance with six votes in favor, Reese abstaining and none opposed.

In July, Planning Director Kaiser described a roughly 245-foot extension of Access Road One across the restaurant property’s frontage, with a 40-foot right of way and a 20-foot utility easement to the north. His June description of the proposed layout placed customer access behind Sheetz: one inbound lane for parking and two for drive-through queues, circulating counterclockwise before exiting onto Access Road One. In July, Engineer Davis said the Planning Commission required delineators, striping and other measures to improve local traffic circulation.

source.title: Special City Council Agenda Packet - Approved Minutes

evidenceRefs.assertion: Council linked Ordinance 26-082 to Chick-fil-A locating in Wadsworth.
evidenceRefs.quote:
He noted that the primary items were Ordinance 26-082 concerning Chick-
fil-A's ability to locate within the City

evidenceRefs.assertion: Ordinance 26-082 accepted Access Road One public right of way and utility easements on the subdivision plat for Wadsworth lot 10300; the Planning Commission approved the plat June 8, 2026.
evidenceRefs.quote:
ORDINANCE NO. 26-082: AN ORDINANCE ACCEPTING PUBLIC RIGHT OF WAY
FOR ACCESS ROAD #1 AND PUBLIC UTILITY EASEMENTS AS SHOWN ON THE
SUBDIVISION PLAT OF CITY OF WADSWORTH LOT #10300 AS APPROVED BY
THE PLANNING COMMISSION ON JUNE 8, 2026 AND DECLARING AN
EMERGENCY

evidenceRefs.assertion: Council adopted Ordinance 26-082 August 3, 2026, with six affirmative votes, Reese abstaining and none opposed; this remains the project's latest evidenced milestone.
evidenceRefs.quote:
President Rospert called for a vote. Ayes: May,
Stugmyer, Berger, Hines, Maxwell, Yurchiak. Abstain: Reese. Nays: None Ordinance No.
26-082 declared to have been adopted August 3, 2026.

evidenceRefs.assertion: Planning Director Kaiser identified the city lot 10300 property as directly west of Sheetz.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Planning Director Kaiser stated that a second item had been added and that an ordinance request had been
sent to the Law Department concerning the acceptance of public right-of-way and utility easements
associated with the subdivision of City Lot 10300. He provided a copy of the draft plat and explained
that the property is directly west of the Sheetz property

evidenceRefs.assertion: Kaiser confirmed the site was behind Sheetz where the Legacy Inn had been located and described an approximately 245-foot Access Road One extension along the Chick-fil-A property.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Council Member Hines asked whether the property was behind the Sheetz property where the Legacy
Inn had been located.

Planning Director Kaiser confirmed that it was and explained that the extension of Access Road One
would run approximately 245 feet, essentially the length of the Chick-fil-A property.

evidenceRefs.assertion: Kaiser's July description included a 40-foot right of way across the frontage and a 20-foot utility easement to the north.
evidenceRefs.quote:
He explained that Access Road One would
be extended across the frontage of the property as a 40-foot right-of-way and that a 20-foot utility
easement to the north would also require Council acceptance.

evidenceRefs.assertion: The site, access-road and traffic-requirement descriptions were reported at the July 13, 2026 meeting.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Council Member Hines called the July 13, 2026 Economic Development & Planning Committee to
order at approximately 5:00 p.m.

evidenceRefs.assertion: Kaiser's June proposed circulation description placed access behind Sheetz, with one parking lane, two drive-through lanes, counterclockwise circulation and exit onto Access Road One.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Director Kaiser confirmed that customers would enter the property from Access Road No. 1 located
behind Sheetz. After entering the site, traffic would separate into three inbound lanes. One lane would
serve the primary parking area, while two lanes would feed the dual drive-through queues. Vehicles
would circulate counterclockwise around the building, with the ordering point located along the north
side nearest Interstate 76 before continuing to the pickup windows and exiting back onto Access Road
No. 1.

evidenceRefs.assertion: The proposed circulation description dates to June 8, 2026.
Engineer Davis said the Planning Commission required Chick-fil-A to install delineators, striping and other measures to optimize local traffic patterns.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Engineer Davis explained that it varies. He cited Chick-fil-A as an example, stating that the Planning
Commission required the project to install delineators, striping, and other measures to optimize local
traffic patterns

review.residentValue: Residents following the proposed Chick-fil-A can locate its site behind Sheetz and understand the proposed vehicle access and required traffic measures alongside the dated August approval.

title: Good Avenue and Longview Drive water-line project cleared for bidding
dek: Wadsworth City Council authorized bidding and contract awards for the Good Avenue and Longview Drive water-line replacement project on September 1, 2026. The action concerns water infrastructure on those two streets.
body:
Wadsworth City Council authorized bidding and contract awards for the Good Avenue and Longview Drive water-line replacement project on September 1, 2026. The action concerns water infrastructure on those two streets.

Council adopted Ordinance 26-095 unanimously, authorizing the public service director to advertise, receive bids and award contracts for the project. This dated milestone establishes the authority to seek bids and award the work; it does not establish a construction start date.

source.title: City Council Agenda Packet & Approved Minutes

evidenceRefs.assertion: Ordinance 26-095 authorizes the public service director to advertise, receive bids and award contracts for water-line replacement on Good Avenue and Longview Drive in Wadsworth. This establishes bidding and award authority rather than a construction start date.
evidenceRefs.quote:
ORDINANCE NO. 26-095: AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING AND DIRECTING THE
DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC SERVICE TO ADVERTISE, RECEIVE BIDS AND AWARD
CONTRACTS PURSUANT TO ORC 735.05 IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE
REQUIREMENTS OF ORC 9.17 FOR THE GOOD AVENUE AND LONGVIEW DRIVE
WATER LINE REPLACEMENT PROJECT AND DECLARING AN EMERGENCY

evidenceRefs.assertion: Council unanimously adopted Ordinance 26-095 on September 1, 2026.
evidenceRefs.quote:
President Pro Tem Stugmyer called for a vote. Ayes: Yurchiak, Maxwell, Hines, Reese,
Stugmyer, Berger, May. Nays: None Ordinance No. 26-095 declared to have been adopted
September 1, 2026.

review.residentValue: Residents along Good Avenue and Longview Drive can identify the September 1 water-line replacement authorization without mistaking it for a construction announcement.

claimChecks.assertion: Council unanimously adopted Ordinance 26-095 on September 1, 2026.
claimChecks.note: Page 5 contains the exact supplied adoption excerpt, naming seven affirmative votes and no opposing votes. Supports the date and unanimity stated in the copy.

claimChecks.assertion: The recorded action establishes authority to seek bids and award contracts, without establishing a construction start date.
claimChecks.note: Page 5 documents authorization, not an executed award or construction schedule. The copy accurately limits what this milestone establishes.

claimChecks.note: The action predates the October 5 cutoff by 34 days. Neither supplied prior item covers this project. The dated lookup framing qualifies under the PROJECT exception without presenting the authorization as fresh news.

title: Wall Road annexation proposal cleared a municipal-services step
dek: Wadsworth City Council adopted a municipal-services resolution on July 14, 2026, for Wall Road Development’s proposed annexation of 94.2835 acres from Wadsworth Township into the city.
body:
Wadsworth City Council adopted a municipal-services resolution on July 14, 2026, for Wall Road Development’s proposed annexation of 94.2835 acres from Wadsworth Township into the city.

Economic Development Director Tom Morris explained that the resolution identifies municipal services available if the property is annexed. He said it did not approve the annexation or a development, or determine the city’s capacity to serve the property. Council adopted Resolution 26-09 with seven votes in favor and none opposed.

source.title: Special City Council Agenda Packet - Approved Minutes

evidenceRefs.assertion: Resolution 26-09 concerns municipal services for Wall Road Development’s proposed annexation of 94.2835 acres from Wadsworth Township into Wadsworth.
evidenceRefs.quote:
RESOLUTION NO. 26-09: A RESOLUTION PURSUANT TO DIVISION (C) OF
SECTION 709.023 OF THE OHIO REVISED CODE STATING WHAT SERVICES THE
CITY OF WADSWORTH WILL PROVIDE AND AN APPROXIMATE DATE BY
WHICH IT WILL PROVIDE THEM TO THE TERRITORY PROPOSED FOR
ANNEXATION BY THE PETITION OF WALL ROAD DEVELOPMENT FOR AN
EXPEDITED TYPE 2 ANNEXATION OF 94.2835 ACRES FROM THE TOWNSHIP OF
WADSWORTH TO THE CITY OF WADSWORTH UPON ANNEXATION

evidenceRefs.assertion: Economic Development Director Morris described the resolution as identifying available services, without approving annexation or development or determining service capacity.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Economic Director Morris explained that the resolution fulfills the City's statutory obligation
under Ohio law to identify the municipal services available to the proposed annexation area
within twenty days of the filing of the petition. He emphasized that the resolution was
procedural and did not constitute approval of the annexation, approval of development, or a
determination regarding the City's capacity to serve the property.

evidenceRefs.assertion: Council adopted Resolution 26-09 on July 14, 2026, with seven affirmative votes and none opposed.
evidenceRefs.quote:
President Rospert called for a vote. Ayes: Berger, Reese, Yurchiak,
Maxwell, May Stugmyer, Hines. Nays: None Resolution No. 26-09 declared to have been
adopted July 14, 2026.

review.residentValue: Residents following the Wall Road Development proposal can distinguish Council’s July 14 services resolution from approval to annex or develop the land.

claimChecks.assertion: Economic Development Director Tom Morris explained that the resolution identifies available municipal services if annexation occurs, without approving annexation or development or determining service capacity.
claimChecks.note: Page 1 identifies Tom Morris as Economic Director; page 3 contains the quoted explanation and conditional service availability. The body appropriately attributes these distinctions to Morris.

claimChecks.assertion: Council adopted Resolution 26-09 on July 14, 2026, with seven affirmative votes and none opposed.
claimChecks.note: Page 4 explicitly records adoption and no opposing votes. Although the final roll call omits a comma between May and Stugmyer, page 1 identifies them as separate members, supporting seven affirmative votes. The earlier divided procedural vote was not the adoption vote.

claimChecks.note: The resolution’s purpose on page 3 and adoption on page 4 support the headline and stage. The copy does not imply annexation approval, construction or an opening date.

title: Briarthorn turn-lane construction was reported beginning in July
dek: Construction was beginning on the State Route 261 turn lane into Briarthorn, Economic Development Director Tom Morris reported on July 13, 2026.
body:
Construction was beginning on the State Route 261 turn lane into Briarthorn, Economic Development Director Tom Morris reported on July 13, 2026.

The improvement was a condition for completing the subdivision. In June, Morris said a developer had committed to building the required lane and that approximately 40 residential lots remained in the principal unfinished section. He explained that the subdivision was already platted and subdivided, allowing remaining homes to proceed to construction once the turn lane was completed.

evidenceRefs.assertion: On July 13, 2026, Morris reported construction beginning on the State Route 261 turn lane into Briarthorn.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Economic Director Morris stated that the City was beginning to enter the building phase of the
construction season. He reported that construction was beginning on State Route 261 for the turn lane
into Briarthorn and that residents would begin seeing construction signs in the area.

evidenceRefs.assertion: The July report occurred at the July 13, 2026 committee meeting.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Council Member Hines called the July 13, 2026 Economic Development & Planning Committee to
order at approximately 5:00 p.m.

evidenceRefs.assertion: The required turn lane connects State Route 261 to Briarthorn Crescent.
evidenceRefs.quote:
a previous Planning Commission required installation of
a left-turn lane from State Route 261 into Briarthorn Crescent once the subdivision exceeded
approximately one hundred homes.

evidenceRefs.assertion: Morris said a developer committed to constructing the required turn lane, allowing completion of the subdivision.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Director Morris stated that a developer has now committed to constructing the required turn lane,
allowing completion of the subdivision.

evidenceRefs.assertion: Approximately 40 residential lots remained in the principal unfinished section, according to Morris.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Director Morris responded that approximately forty additional residential lots remain within the
principal unfinished section of Briarthorn.

evidenceRefs.assertion: Morris explained that the subdivision was already platted and subdivided and remaining homes could proceed to construction once the lane was completed.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Director Morris explained that the subdivision has already been platted and subdivided; therefore,
once the turn lane is completed, the remaining homes may proceed directly to construction.

evidenceRefs.assertion: The earlier development report occurred June 8, 2026.
evidenceRefs.quote:
Council Member May called the Economic Development & Planning Committee Work Session to
order at 5:00 p.m.
